jobs.jd: 🚀 Build the data layer AI needs to do science Application deadline: 16 Nov 2026 23:59 CET About Claims AI ate the Internet, but it can't digest science yet. A paper is thousands of words of prose written for humans, but an AI agent doing research needs to know what was claimed, what evidence supports it, and how far to trust it. Claims turns the scientific literature into exactly that: every claim, tied to its evidence, as structured data that models and agents can query. We're a startup and run as Subnet 111 on Bittensor. Since our mainnet launch on 28 August 2026, an open competition of miners has processed more than 10,000 papers, and every record was checked by our validator before it entered the dataset. The competition keeps raising the bar: miners keep finding ways to beat our own reference pipeline, and every win becomes part of the standard the whole network is scored against. The team Claims was founded by two professors of economics and a senior engineer. Philipp Koellinger , CEO, is a professor of economics and an experienced entrepreneur: founder of DeSci Labs and the DeSci Foundation, and co-builder of SciWeave with Ogban. Christian Roessler , co-founder, is a professor of economics and game theorist. He designs the incentive mechanism that makes the miner competition work. Ogban Ugot , engineering, is a senior backend and machine learning engineer. He built SciWeave, the Claims miner, validator and data pipeline, and you will work with him every day. You would be the fourth person on the team and our second engineer. Our culture We are a fully remote team spread across Europe, Africa and the US West Coast. We have a flat hierarchy and move fast towards clearly defined goals. We think deep, don't shy away from difficult problems or conversations, and we ship relentlessly. The code you will write will run on a live network within your first weeks, and you own real things from day one. jobs.jd: We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want. You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models. Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week. How it works Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another. With our product brands Immoviewer and DocuSketch, we have become one of the most successful and fastest-growing software vendors in the rapidly expanding property tech sector. Our enthusiastic customer base is located across Europe and North America. DocuSketch's groundbreaking digital technology greatly facilitates real estate companies and building restoration companies to digitize, visualize, and virtualize real estate properties. Our solutions help our clients realize tremendous cost-saving potentials, process optimization, and revenue growth. You’ll be working in a team that drives the company's AI development to develop algorithms for a variety of different use cases. This includes e.g. working with equirectangular, phone, or satellite images to detect doors, windows, or other objects inside of buildings or finding facets on the roof. You’ll be challenged by solving complex 3D geometry problems and working closely with our labeling team to ensure the best possible data quality. Responsibilities and Duties: · Research, train and deploy state-of-the-art machine learning models for object detection and 3D perception on equirectangular images · Quickly prototype new ideas/technologies to create proof of concept and demos Qualifications: · Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience · Excellent math skills · Experience with 3D computer vision algorithms · Preferably 5+ years of experience developing and training machine learning models · Strong Experience with Deep ML frameworks (PyTorch) · Strong Experience in Python · Self-motivated and energetic team player with a strong work ethic and cooperative attitude · Excellent communication and organizational skills Plus: · Familiarity with building big data systems · Training very large models using multiple GPUs in the cloud · Experience with training machine learning models on equirectangular images We are seeking a performance-driven, high-energy personality who has several years of experience in the field. Since you will work intensely with teams from many countries solid command of the English language is a prerequisite. We offer attractive compensation, unlimited career opportunities, and the possibility to work in one of the most exciting software companies in the industry. The position will be remote in any location of choice in Europe (outside Russia, Belarus, and Ukraine). Our headquarters are in Berlin, Germany, with major offices in Belgrade, Serbia, Lakeland, Florida, and in Canada. We look forward to receiving your application! Please mention the word **REGAL** and tag RMTM1LjIzMi4yMDAuMzU= when applying to show you read the job post completely (#RMTM1LjIzMi4yMDAuMzU=). This is a beta feature to avoid spam applicants. jobs.jd: About Phaidra Phaidra is building the future of industrial automation. The world today is filled with static, monolithic infrastructure. Factories, power plants, buildings, etc. operate the same they've operated for decades — because the controls programming is hard-coded. Thousands of lines of rules and heuristics that define how the machines interact with each other. The result of all this hard-coding is that facilities are frozen in time, unable to adapt to their environment while their performance slowly degrades. Phaidra creates AI-powered control systems for the industrial sector, enabling industrial facilities to automatically learn and improve over time. Specifically: We use reinforcement learning algorithms to provide this intelligence, converting raw sensor data into high-value actions and decisions. We focus on industrial applications, which tend to be well-sensorized with measurable KPIs — perfect for reinforcement learning. We enable domain experts (our users) to configure the AI control systems (i.e. agents) without writing code. They define what they want their AI agents to do, and we do it for them. Our team has a track record of applying AI to some of the toughest problems. From achieving superhuman performance with DeepMind's AlphaGo, to reducing the energy required to cool Google's Data Centers by 40%, we deeply understand AI and how to apply it in production for massive impact. Phaidra’s ability to achieve its mission is determined by our ability to work together — as defined by our core values: Transparency, Collaboration, Operational Excellence, Ownership, and Empathy.
